memo.verdict: Bullish; progress to Early-Stage; conviction medium, a working hypothesis on the governance question. The record calls flatexDEGIRO (FTK-DE) a 'Major Corporate Change' case that has reached full output and is priced as though the output were about to reverse. The gate line passes: management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4) C, business quality (E 2, BB 2) B, predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) A, trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) A; no D or F, so the case is not parked. The entry: the case clears the 20 percent bar at eighteen months at EUR 28.0 on the modal path (its clearing price is EUR 29.1) and at three years below EUR 26.2. Two dated tests: the Q3 2026 figures (October 2026) and the February 2027 mid-term plan with the Supervisory Board appointments; the record would size the position to the second. The one unresolved question, the September 2026 governance reshuffle, has a date: February 2027, and the June 2027 AGM at the latest for the board seats. What would make the record change sides at thesis level: two consecutive quarters of acquisition cost above EUR 200 per account, or customer growth below 8 percent a year.
case: - The thesis. flatexDEGIRO is a 'Major Corporate Change' case that has reached full output and is priced as though the output were about to reverse. A new chief executive closed a two-year regulatory chapter on his first day (BaFin's special commissioner left 30-Sep-24; Behrens started 01-Oct-24) and reset the cost base of a fixed-cost, scale-driven business, so that revenue growth of 22.2 percent in H1 2026 became net income growth of 41.1 percent. At EUR 28.0 the shares stand at 10.1x consensus earnings 24 months forward, a 41 percent discount to Avanza and Nordnet, and what the price charges for is a three-week-old governance reshuffle and a slowdown in new-customer additions, not the earnings already reported.

- The change is internal, multi-dimensional and in the accounts. The screen's rule is met twice over: a chief-executive change plus repeated guidance increases, and at least five internal forces strong. Cost base: personnel -21 percent to EUR 24.1m in Q2 2026, operating expenses -1.0 percent to EUR 59.6m on revenue +26 percent, headcount 1,210 at end-2025 against 1,271. Guidance: the 2027 targets (EUR 650m revenue, EUR 200m net income) pulled into 2026 on 26-Jun-26; FY2026 net income raised on 22-Jul-26 to EUR 200m to EUR 230m. Capital returns: a seven-fold dividend step to EUR 0.30, a 20 percent payout, a EUR 50m buyback completed May 2025 (3,136,243 shares at EUR 15.94, 2.8 percent of capital). Products: crypto, securities lending, fractional savings plans, deposits-as-a-service (EUR 1.0bn of deposits by 30-Jun-26), the pension account for 01-Jan-27. Standards (A): every BaFin finding remediated, SREP surcharge cut from 4.25 percent to 2.50 percent, adjusted reporting dropped, IFRS 18 early, remuneration caps with malus and clawback approved by 93.46 percent.

- The external forces net to a modest tailwind against one large headwind. Tailwinds, real but small in near-term earnings: the Altersvorsorgedepot (approved May 2026, live 01-Jan-27, aiming to double retail equity participation to 28m and mobilise over EUR 3 trillion; Deutsche Bank puts FY2027 fee income at EUR 1m); the PFOF ban (in force in Germany from July 2026, low single-digit percent of group revenue exposed, competitors reliant on it); the ECB rate rise from 2.00 to 2.25 percent in June 2026, on EUR 6.5bn of customer cash paid nothing. The headwind (D): Trade Republic at 10m customers and an EUR 11bn valuation with 3 percent on cash in Finland; Scalable's PRIME+; Nordnet entering Germany in H2 2026; FinecoBank's pan-European brokerage; neobrokers spending ten to twenty times the marketing budget; gross additions -12.3 percent at a doubled acquisition cost. The installed base is compounding while the funnel narrows: accounts +11.1 percent, assets +29.7 percent, 100 percent of EUR 5.16bn of inflows invested.
counter_case: - At thesis level: the FY2025 and H1 2026 profits are a cyclical peak dressed as a structural change. Trading activity per customer ran at 25.1 annualised trades in H1 2026 against 23.0 in FY2025 and 22.0 in FY2024; interest income is lifted by EUR 6.5bn of deposits on which the company pays nothing; both are cyclical. The peak masks a structural slowdown in customer acquisition: gross additions -12.3 percent in H1 2026, acquisition cost EUR 171 per account in Q1 2026 against EUR 86, against neobrokers spending ten to twenty times more. When activity normalises the operating leverage runs in reverse, FY2027 consensus of EUR 2.40 is cut, and the multiple, already at a discount, falls toward the 2022 trough of 8.7x. The record concedes the cyclical component (it models FY2027 at +12 percent, not +29 percent, and puts no re-rating beyond the ten-year median at odds above even) and answers that the slowdown is in gross additions not the installed base (accounts +11.1 percent to 3.66m; inflows EUR 5.16bn against EUR 5.56bn, 100 percent invested), that the cost base is structural (headcount 1,210 against 1,271; personnel EUR 24.1m, -21 percent; the AI call centre complete; the platform merger dated), and that 10.1x already discounts a normalisation that has not begun (August 2026 trades +17 percent). Change of side: two consecutive quarters of acquisition cost above EUR 200, or customer growth below 8 percent a year.

- At foundations level: the business is a rate-and-volatility beneficiary dressed as a platform. Sixty to 80 percent of revenue is transactional; the interest income rests on paying 0 percent on EUR 6.5bn of customer cash; neither is defended by anything a competitor cannot copy with enough capital (Trade Republic's 3 percent on cash in Finland; Scalable's EUR 500k deposit cover). The record concedes the deposit franchise is the fragile part: a deposit rate war would cut net interest income quickly and the company has no hedge. It holds on the cost side (EUR 1.45 a trade against EUR 5 to EUR 10; a 48.5 to 55.1 percent EBITDA margin; a 22.1 percent return on invested capital) and on the customers (retention 98.3 percent; accounts +11 percent; cash +28 percent in three years of neobroker spending; the licence, the custody and the German tax plumbing as switching costs). It holds less firmly on the value chain: the industry structure is a D.
triggers: - Governance (Key Risk): the board search; the February 2027 plan; the dual structure's accountability. Modal: seats filled with credible independents by the June 2027 AGM, about 70 percent. Alarm: no appointments announced with the February 2027 figures. Invalidate: seats unfilled or filled with founder associates by the June 2027 AGM, or a transformational acquisition announced before the board is complete; also, the shared chief-executive structure producing contradictory guidance.

- Cost drop-through (Key Driver): Q2 2026 operating expenses EUR 59.6m, personnel EUR 24.1m. Modal: brokers'-basis EBITDA margin 54.2 percent FY2026, 57.0 percent FY2028 (consensus 53.9 and 59.2). Alarm: a quarter with operating expenses above EUR 70m without a stated reason. Invalidate: FY2026 net income below EUR 200m.

- Installed base growth and activity (Key Driver): 10 percent customer growth and +17 percent trades in August 2026. Modal: customer growth about 10 percent a year, trades per customer 23 to 25, plausible at about 60 percent. Alarm: customer growth below 9 percent or trades per customer below 22 for two months. Invalidate: customer growth below 8 percent a year.

- Neobroker competition and acquisition cost (Key Risk): EUR 96 in Q2 2026, EUR 171 in Q1. Modal: EUR 90 to EUR 130 a quarter through 2027, higher around the pension launch. Alarm: above EUR 150 in any quarter. Invalidate: above EUR 200 for two consecutive quarters. Watch Nordnet's German launch in H2 2026 and competitor deposit-rate moves.

- Deposit margin and treasury yield (Key Driver): EUR 6.51bn of customer cash; EUR 1.3bn of bonds at 2.3 percent; ECB 2.25 percent; interest income EUR 52.7m in Q2 2026. Alarm: an ECB cut below 2.00 percent, or a competitor paying interest on cash in Germany or the Netherlands at scale. Invalidate: a net interest margin on deposits below 0.70 percent.

- Pension reform: accounts from January 2027; modal 200,000 to 300,000 by end-2027 against a company target of 400,000 to 600,000 at a 4 percent share. Alarm: no account disclosure by the H1 2027 report. Invalidate: fewer than 300,000 cumulative by December 2027.
